name: The Wilhelmina Chestnut of Noordereiland

location.address: Burgemeester Hoffmanplein, corner of Van der Takstraat, Noordereiland, Rotterdam

access: Free, open public square (Burgemeester Hoffmanplein) on Noordereiland; no hours.
transport: Noordereiland is reached over the Koninginnebrug from Rotterdam Centrum; walking time from the nearest metro stop not verified.

location_site.name: Burgemeester Hoffmanplein (small square with the Wilhelmina fountain)

verify_notes: Alive per noordereiland.org, 26 June 2026 (updated 30 Sept 2026): the chestnut stands but is in poor health (chestnut bleeding canker plus two life-threatening fungi on the trunk); a large main branch broke off some years ago and was saved by tree surgeons; expected to become a safety risk and be removed 'in a few years'. Not yet removed. Girth 'almost 4 m', height 18-24 m (noordereiland.org, citing tree knight Pim Janse; same figures on the 2022 page). Age disputed: register planted_band 1880-1890 and register history 'planted 1898 for Wilhelmina's accession'; noordereiland.org 2026 says planted 1889 for the inauguration; noordereiland.org 2022 says 'from 1870'; nl.wikipedia says probably planted 1898 with the fountain. Wilhelmina was inaugurated in 1898, so 1889 reads as a typo. Derived age is broad, from the register band plus the 1898 claim; not sharpened. WWII story (register and noordereiland.org agree): known to resistance people as the 'dubbele paardenkastanje' (double chestnut), a Wilhelmina tree residents guarded as a quiet act of resistance; a second story told that it grew on ground where the dead were buried so better not cut; elders in the 1970s said 'come back when it flowers, then you see two flowers'; survived the fighting around Noordereiland and the Maas bridges and the Hunger Winter when trees were felled for fuel; a tale says someone tried to fell it and gave up after one branch. Its roots cracked the Wilhelmina fountain (Evers design, 1898) in the early 1990s; fountain removed, restored and replaced a century after the inauguration (nl.wikipedia). Flowers April-May (noordereiland.org). A second chestnut on the same square opposite the Lelieblok, planted 1920, girth almost 3 m, height 15-18 m, good health, is the SMALLER one; the subject is the larger one at the corner of Van der Takstraat beside the fountain. Pin: register coordinate (nr 1691895, n_trees 1), not checked on aerial imagery; OSM natural=tree nodes on the square carry no species, so approximate. Covered-country rule (NL): no photo and no confirmed pin, so strictly a lead; delivered as flagged for the orchestrator's gate. Commons geosearch within 100 m found no tree photo; lifecheck NONE.
